correctness.rationale: Conditional on X_n=x, the p-th moment reduces to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral with quadratic coefficient δ=1−phq(x), q=σ²x²/(1+x)³: it is finite iff δ>0. The maximum q(2)=4σ²/27 gives uniform subcritical all-iterate finiteness. The first-step log-multiplier is a strictly convex Gaussian quadratic with lower support below 2 for every x0, and yields a strictly positive density near x=2. Above critical phσ²=27/4, an open set of X1 values has infinite conditional p-moment. At criticality δ(x)=(x−2)²/12+O((x−2)³) and the finite-case conditional moment grows as exp(c/(x−2)²), nonintegrably against that density. Jensen propagates infinite moments for all n≥2. The underlying Lipschitz diffusion has finite finite-time moments. Independent symbolic identities and Gaussian quadratures passed 36 tests.
